'''Telettoh's Maxim''' was a doctrine that was adopted by many starship crews in the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] following the [[Jedi Civil War]]. It stated that starships should not take any [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lords]] aboard due to their perceived destructive tendencies. The doctrine was first coined by the [[Republic Navy/Legends|Republic Navy]] [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Telettoh]] who had unknowingly carried the future Sith Lord [[Darth Malak]] aboard his [[Hammerhead-class cruiser|''Hammerhead''-class cruiser]] ''[[Testament]]''. At that time, Malak was a member of a Jedi faction known as the [[Revanchist]]s who advocated a hardline stance against the [[Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders/Legends|Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders]]. Telettoh would spend the rest of his career trying to undo the damage caused by his actions.

[[1032 BBY/Legends|Millennia later]], the mercenary leader [[Jarrow Rusher]] would cite Telettoh's Maxim as an argument against the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Kerra Holt]]'s decision to bring the captive Sith Lord [[Quillan (Sith)|Quillan]] aboard his ship [[Diligence (New Sith Wars)|''Diligence'']]. Following their [[Battle of Byllura|escape]] from the Sith world of [[Byllura]], Rusher accused Kerra of trying to endanger the lives of his crew by bringing a Dark Sider aboard. However, Quillan did not pose a threat to the crew and passengers due to his mentally challenged state and infantile upbringing.
